title: CSV in, JSON out
description:
Convert between the formats of lesson 6.02:

```python
def read_people(csv_text): ...     # -> (people, errors): people is a list of {"name": str, "age": int, "city": str}
def to_json(people): ...           # pretty JSON: indent 2, keys sorted, non-ASCII characters kept as they are
def write_csv(people): ...         # CSV text with the header name,age,city and one row per person (lines end with \n)
```

`read_people` reads CSV with a header row (the columns may be in any order; extra columns are ignored). A row whose age is not a whole number is skipped and reported as `"row N: bad age <text>"`, where N counts the data rows from 1. Missing columns in the header: return `([], ["missing column: <name>"])` for the first missing of `name`, `age`, `city`. Use the `csv` module (names and cities may contain commas and quotes).
hints: `csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text))` reads CSV from a string; `reader.fieldnames` is the header (None for empty input).

`csv.DictWriter` quotes fields that need it; pass `lineterminator="
"` so lines end with `
` instead of `
`.
